learning: Increased base speed and PID gains to improve responsiveness and control precision, compensating for earlier line loss and off-track failures. Adjusted sensor weights on rear sensors to better exploit earlier turn detection from moved rear sensors.
notes: Controller tuned to leverage improved early turn detection from rear sensors moved further back to y=-0.035 and stable wide wheel track of 0.18. Increased base speed and PID gains to improve progress and reduce line loss events observed in last iteration. Sensor weights on rear sensors increased in magnitude to enhance corrective steering.
rationale: The previous iteration's geometry with rear sensors at y=-0.03 and wheel track 0.18 improved stability and early turn detection but still resulted in early off-track failures and one line loss event per run. Moving rear sensors further back to y=-0.035 should provide even earlier line information, allowing the controller to react sooner to sharp turns. To exploit this, I increased base speed from 0.15 to 0.155 and PID gains (kp from 0.22 to 0.23, ki from 0.025 to 0.03, kd from 0.045 to 0.05) to improve responsiveness and control precision. Sensor weights on the rear sensors were increased in magnitude (from -0.2 to -0.25) to strengthen their influence on steering corrections. These changes aim to reduce line loss events, improve progress and completion rates, and maintain stability on the wider wheel track. I preserved the sensor size at 0.016 for noise robustness and kept other geometry parameters unchanged. I request the same measurements as before to verify improvements.
